answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a fixed period before it may claim rewards. The protocol caps rewards per verified work unit and slashes the stake when identities coordinate duplicate claims, with challenges settled by independent agents. Splitting one operator into many accounts then yields no extra reward, while detection burns capital and liquidity; even at the nadir, a haven for honest newcomers need not become a velvet pass for cheap aliases.
